question.text: Mr. Verma invested Rs. 6,00,000 in a gold ETF in January 2023. He redeemed the units in March 2025 (after 26 months) for Rs. 8,50,000. What is his tax liability including cess? (Assume he is in the 30% tax bracket)

answer.text: Rs. 78,000 (30% slab rate on Rs. 2,50,000 + 4% cess, treating as STCG)
Rs. 16,250 (12.5% on Rs. 1,25,000 after Rs. 1.25 lakh LTCG exemption + 4% cess)
Rs. 52,000 (20% with indexation on Rs. 2,50,000 + 4% cess)

explanation.text: The Logic: For a Gold ETF purchased before 1 April 2023, the workbook states that profit on units held for more than 12 months is treated as long-term capital gain. Mr. Verma held the units for 26 months, so the gain qualifies as LTCG. LTCG = 8,50,000 - 6,00,000 = Rs. 2,50,000. Applying the 12.5% LTCG rate from the summary table: tax = 2,50,000 x 12.5% = Rs. 31,250. Adding 4% Health and Education cess: 31,250 x 1.04 = Rs. 32,500. The Trap: Option A wrongly applies slab rate by treating the gain as STCG. Option C incorrectly applies the Rs. 1.25 lakh exemption, which under Section 112A is available only for equity-oriented schemes, not for gold ETFs. Option D applies 20% with indexation, which is no longer the applicable rate under the post-Budget 2024 regime reflected in the workbook. Note: Source - NISM Series X-B Investment Adviser (Level 2) workbook, Gold ETF section and summary tax table (pp. 255 and 287-288). The Gold ETF passage uses a "more than 12 months" long-term holding rule.
